summary: Console usage attribution and scheduled alerts misaligned after retention compaction merges involving archived API keys
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that over the weekend a retention compaction job merged old partitions that included several archived API keys. After the compaction, the console shows a sudden drop in usage attributed to the active API key and spikes attributed to an 'archived' api_key_id. Scheduled alerts that rely on route-level usage thresholds also fired incorrectly (false-positive) because the post-compaction attribution window considered the archived keys in the same rollup bucket.

Impact:
- MapleHealth reported a spurious billing alert and two high-priority on-call pages overnight.
- Scheduled alerts for usage thresholds fired for a route that had no active traffic.
- Trace links (tracehook context) attached to the alert were missing or pointed to the archived api_key, making debugging difficult.

Environment:
prod-us-east cluster; retention compaction run id rc-20260307-03; org id: org-7891; route id: route-33; affected API keys: api_abc_old_443 (archived), api_maple_primary_2 (active).

Steps to reproduce (customer provided):
1) Run usage report for route-33 for 2026-03-06 to 2026-03-08 in console time range UTC.
2) Compare per-api-key attribution before and after rc-20260307-03 compaction job.
3) Observe scheduled alert history for route-33 that fired at 2026-03-07T04:12:00Z.

Observed behavior:
- Hourly rollups show a drop of ~95% for api_maple_primary_2 for 2026-03-07 03:00-04:00Z and a compensating spike attributed to api_abc_old_443 in the same hour.
- Alert evaluation history shows the alert condition evaluated on compacted rollup records and attached trace_anchor referencing api_abc_old_443 (archived) which has no live tracehooks.

Expected behavior:
- Compaction should preserve correct api-key attribution and not reassign recent active traffic to archived identifiers.
- Alerts should evaluate against rollups that maintain route-to-active-api-key mapping for the alert time window.

Customer logs/attachments:
- CSV export of pre/post compaction rollup diffs (attached by customer).
steps_to_reproduce: Download hourly-usage rollups for route-33 for 2026-03-06..2026-03-08 from console export
Re-run rc-20260307-03 compaction locally against a small dataset (dev cluster) following runbook
Compare attribution by api_key_id across pre/post compaction datasets
Inspect alert-eval history for scheduled alerts on route-33 in the same timeframe and check alert.attach.trace_anchor
observed_behavior: Active api key usage dropped ~95% in the post-compaction hourly rollup
Archived api key shows compensating spike in same hour
Alert evaluation attached trace anchors pointing to archived api key which has no live traces
expected_behavior: Attribution remains stable across compaction boundaries
Alerts attach tracehooks that map to active api keys and include trace context
No spurious billing or alert pages due to compaction metadata merges
comments: 2026-03-10 | Ariana Patel (Support): Customer submitted CSV diffs and a screenshot of the alert history. Provided compaction run id. Asked for triage and impact assessment.
2026-03-10 | Ethan Park (Oncall): Acknowledged receipt. Marked as P1 Sev1 due to billing/alert pages. Requested logs from retention service and list of affected partitions.

2026-03-11 | SRE - Miguel Alvarez: Early hypothesis: compaction merge used deprecated api_key canonicalization map which recently changed during migration; might be reassigning api_key_ids to a historical canonical id for archived keys. Pulling compaction job logs (rc-20260307-03).

2026-03-12 | Eng - Priya Singh: Found compaction job used schema v2 rollup-merger; a fallback path executed for partitions > 30 days that uses legacy attribution index. Placed a patch to skip legacy index for partitions with recent timestamps. Opening PR #2187.
2026-03-13 | Support (Ariana): Customer confirmed they got follow-up pages for the same alert; asked for ETA on fix and whether manual remediation is possible.
investigation_notes: Compaction job rc-20260307-03 logs show fallback to legacy-canonicalization when merge conflicts detected at bucket-level.
Legacy canonicalization index contains entries mapping api_maple_primary_2 -> api_abc_old_443 for historical reasons (API key rotate path).
Alert evaluator reads aggregated rollups by bucket timestamp; it does not re-run attribution reconciliation post-compaction which allows the misattributed records to trigger alerts.
Tracehook linkage requires api_key to be present in active key registry to resolve trace anchors; archived keys are not present resulting in missing trace context.
Reproduced locally: running compaction with legacy index on a small dataset produced identical misattribution pattern and caused test alert to fire.
resolution_notes: Temporary mitigation: disabled scheduled compaction fallback to legacy canonicalization for in-flight jobs (flag rc.fallback_legacy=false). Rolled back rc-20260307-03 indices for 2026-03-07 by restoring pre-compact S3 snapshot for affected partitions and re-running a safe compaction job using schema v3 merge logic. PR github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/2187 contains the permanent fix to skip legacy index merges for buckets with any records < 14 days old. Recommended follow-ups: (1) run backfill to reconcile attribution for 2026-02-22..2026-03-08 windows, (2) add unit test for canonicalization map fallback, (3) postmortem to explain why legacy index entries remained for org-7891. Customer notified 2026-03-13 and asked to validate reconciled usage; they confirmed reduced false alerts but requested completion of backfill and confirmation of billing adjustments.
outcome: Mitigation applied and pre-compaction rollups restored for the affected hour; customer reported alerts stopped firing incorrectly. Follow-up backfill scheduled and owner assigned to Eng (Priya Singh). Billing team notified to review possible credit for spurious alerts/pages.
